scale.interpretation: A position between the named low and high poles. Ranges are experiment hypotheses, not token values, visual measurements, or approved scores.

provenance.evidenceScope: Current official public surfaces from Notion, Linear, Stripe, ElevenLabs, and Ramp, captured or reviewed on 20 July 2026.
limitations: The five-source panel is narrow and software-heavy.
There is no dedicated anti-reference or broad cross-category cohort.
Advertising, email, authenticated product UI, and small-size evidence are incomplete.
Motion semantics are better evidenced than duration, easing, responsive motion, or reduced-motion implementation.
Product modulation is a hypothesis based on the current Mez product jobs and must be tested in monochrome prototypes.
No source value, token, asset, composition, or signature may be transferred into Mez production from this file.
provenance.forbiddenUse: Do not average these ranges into a style score, use them to clone a source, or promote them without the stated human gate and tests.

dimensions.name: Recognition resilience
dimensions.definition: How strongly an output remains attributable to Mez when the wings, company name, product name, gradients, and other obvious identifiers are removed.

lowPole.label: Single-device and generic
lowPole.description: Recognition collapses without a mark, colour core, or familiar SaaS treatment.

highPole.label: Distributed and resilient
highPole.description: Composition, evidence order, relationship geometry, type hierarchy, state language, and motion purpose reinforce one authorship independently.

desiredRange.rationale: Mez needs strong authorship across channels without forcing one visual device into every output.

channelModulation.rationale: Long-form surfaces can repeat several recognition behaviours.
State language, relationships, controls, and evidence framing should carry authorship without decoration.
A small placement may expose fewer behaviours, but at least two non-colour cues should remain.
Recognition must survive client constraints and image blocking.
Evidence hierarchy, annotation, and relationship geometry should identify the system in restrained print-like contexts.

productModulation.rationale: The live flagship should establish the shared operating grammar most completely.
Campaign expression may vary more, but evidence and relationship behaviour must retain Mez authorship.
Data framing, provenance, and comparison behaviour can become strong non-colour identifiers.
Technical objects should remain recognisably Mez rather than defaulting to generic developer-tool styling.

dimensions.confidence: high for the mechanism, untested for Mez authorship
tensions: Current gradient equity versus logo-free resilience

tests.method: Run E-01 on five monochrome, logo-free outputs.
tests.passCondition: Reviewers group the family above chance and do not repeatedly attribute it to one source brand.

tests.method: Remove one recognition behaviour at a time.
tests.passCondition: No single removal collapses authorship or product comprehension.

approvalGate.requiredEvidence: Blind authorship results, originality review, and cross-channel specimens

dimensions.name: Restraint to expressiveness
dimensions.definition: How much visual energy, contrast, illustration, colour, motion, and compositional surprise an output uses after clarity and proof requirements are met.

lowPole.label: Severely restrained
lowPole.description: Neutral, sparse, low-chrome presentation with expression carried mainly by hierarchy and behaviour.

highPole.label: Strongly expressive
highPole.description: High-energy colour, imagery, motion, contrast, and composition create an emotionally prominent surface.

desiredRange.rationale: Mez should feel premium and ownable without becoming anonymous minimal software or generic AI spectacle.

channelModulation.rationale: Marketing can establish emotional territory while yielding to literal proof.
Operational comprehension and control should dominate persistent use.
Compact promotion benefits from stronger focal energy, bounded by one proof object.
Expression must survive client fallbacks and preserve the next action.
Analytical trust, scan, printing, and reuse favour restraint.

productModulation.rationale: The flagship should feel calm enough for orchestration and expressive enough to establish the family.
Advertising work permits higher campaign energy, provided performance proof and controls remain legible.
Analytical interpretation benefits from restraint and selective emphasis.
Technical proof should lead, while avoiding anonymous dark-tool minimalism.

tests.method: Render low, middle, and high expression variants with identical approved content.
tests.passCondition: The selected range improves recognition and preference without reducing claim comprehension or originality.
Essential hierarchy, product territory, and proof remain intact.

approvalGate.requiredEvidence: Cross-channel visual territories, accessibility review, and source-signature review

dimensions.name: Editorial to operational density
dimensions.definition: How much information, control, state, annotation, and evidence is visible at once, with density determined by receiver intent and the information object.

lowPole.label: Editorial calm
lowPole.description: One main idea, generous orientation, few controls, and shallow evidence depth.

highPole.label: Operational inspection
highPole.description: Multiple objects, states, controls, exceptions, ownership, provenance, and comparison are visible for action.

desiredRange.rationale: The system needs several governed density modes rather than one preferred midpoint.

channelModulation.rationale: Begin with orientation, then increase density at evaluation points.
Objects, state, control, ownership, and exceptions must remain inspectable.
One claim, one proof object, and one outcome marker should dominate.
Retain context, changed state, consequence, and next action.
Data, method, uncertainty, source, and comparison support evaluation and reuse.

productModulation.rationale: Orchestration requires several work streams while maintaining a clear system overview.
Campaign creation needs visual focus, while performance and approvals add operational depth.
Comparison, trends, filters, methodology, and uncertainty are core product material.
Plans, files, diffs, runs, logs, exceptions, and review create high task density.

dimensions.confidence: high for channel modulation, medium for product ranges
tensions: Calm shell versus operational scan speed

tests.method: Run E-03 with one proof record across five density modes.
tests.passCondition: Each receiver identifies the claim, evidence class, source, result, and action within the target inspection time.

tests.method: Test responsive grouping and accessible reading order at each density.
tests.passCondition: No essential relationship, control, qualifier, or source is lost at supported widths.

approvalGate.owner: human design lead with content and accessibility review
approvalGate.requiredEvidence: Five-channel transformation, scan test, and responsive review

dimensions.name: Proof literalness
dimensions.definition: How directly a claim is connected to an inspectable input, system action, state change, result, provenance, and control.

lowPole.label: Atmospheric assertion
lowPole.description: The claim relies on decoration, logos, quotes, vague screenshots, or unsupported language.

highPole.label: Inspectable evidence chain
highPole.description: The receiver can see what entered, what happened, what changed, what resulted, where it came from, and what can be controlled.

desiredRange.rationale: Literal proof is the strongest cross-source answer to generic AI and software claims.

channelModulation.rationale: Major claims should sit beside the exact mechanism and result.
The real object, state, control, and provenance are available directly.
Compact formats may show a subset, but the proof class and one literal object must remain.
Context, changed state, result, and source path should survive compression.
Method, uncertainty, date, source, and evidence class are mandatory.

productModulation.rationale: System-wide orchestration claims need visible activity, ownership, result, and review.
Generated creative claims need input, transformation, approval, deployment, and performance evidence.
Analytics must expose data, method, comparison, uncertainty, and source.
Technical claims should resolve to plan, command, file, diff, test, and human decision.

tests.method: Map each claim to the canonical proof record and evidence class.
tests.passCondition: No decorative UI, customer quote, or aggregate statistic impersonates another evidence class.

tests.method: Ask a reviewer to identify input, action, changed state, result, provenance, and control.
tests.passCondition: All fields required by the claim are visible or resolve through an explicit path.

approvalGate.gate: H2 for grammar, per-claim approval for publication
approvalGate.owner: product, content, and human claim owner
approvalGate.requiredEvidence: Real Mez proof record, evidence-class validation, and provenance

dimensions.name: Family coherence to product distinction
dimensions.definition: How the system balances shared parent semantics and controls with product-owned jobs, objects, proof, density, motion, and campaign posture.

lowPole.label: Uniform reskins
lowPole.description: Products share almost everything and differ mainly by name, copy, screenshot, or colour.

highPole.label: Independent mini-brands
highPole.description: Products use unrelated language, components, behaviours, and identities with weak parent recognition.

desiredRange.rationale: The target is a visible shared chassis with substantial product-owned territory, not either extreme.

channelModulation.rationale: Portfolio pages can compare shared family and product-specific jobs directly.
Core controls and state semantics should remain strongly shared while work objects differ.
Campaign work needs a clear product territory plus compact parent attribution.
Product context should be obvious without losing sender trust.
Parent evidence conventions remain shared while data objects and result types identify the product.

productModulation.rationale: The flagship should demonstrate the common chassis and broad orchestration territory.
Campaign creation, approval, deployment, and performance need a visibly distinct proof territory.
Analytical objects, comparison behaviour, and evidence depth should distinguish Prism.
Code, files, diffs, tests, and review create a distinct technical territory within shared Mez controls.

dimensions.confidence: high for axes, medium for desired ranges
tensions: Small-size parent attribution versus product cue

tests.method: Run E-02 with names and product colours removed.
tests.passCondition: All four products remain related and distinguishable by job, object, proof, density, and state.

tests.method: Swap proof objects between product specimens.
tests.passCondition: An inappropriate swap creates an obvious semantic failure rather than remaining visually plausible.

approvalGate.requiredEvidence: Four-product territory contracts and monochrome contact sheet

dimensions.name: Motion semantics
dimensions.definition: How strongly movement communicates system state, ownership, permission, progress, transformation, synchronisation, exception, handoff, completion, or reversal.

lowPole.label: Ambient and ornamental
lowPole.description: Movement creates atmosphere but carries no necessary state information.

highPole.label: State-dependent and informative
highPole.description: Motion makes a specific transition, owner, timing relationship, or result easier to understand.

desiredRange.rationale: Every approved product motion should earn attention by communicating state.

channelModulation.rationale: Demonstrations may animate transformation, but should retain static meaning.
Persistent motion must explain feedback, progress, ownership, or state.
Short motion may attract attention, but one state transition should remain clear.
Most email should rely on static states and robust fallbacks.
Static sequence and annotation are primary; digital reports may use optional explanatory transitions.

productModulation.rationale: Routing, waiting, handoff, verification, exception, and completion define orchestration.
Generation, selection, approval, deployment, and performance change can drive motion meaning.
Filtering, comparison, threshold change, and time progression should remain measured and optional.
Plan, execution, file change, test, failure, review, and rollback form a strong state model.

dimensions.confidence: medium for semantics, low for visual timing specifications
tensions: Shared state semantics versus product-specific expression

tests.method: Run E-04 with static, animated, and reduced-motion versions.
tests.passCondition: State and ownership are correctly identified in every version.

tests.method: Remove the motion from each transition.
tests.passCondition: If comprehension does not decrease, classify the motion as optional atmosphere and do not treat it as a system rule.

approvalGate.owner: human design lead with accessibility review
approvalGate.requiredEvidence: State vocabulary, four product storyboards, and reduced-motion equivalents

dimensions.name: Human control visibility
dimensions.definition: How visibly the system communicates source, permission, current owner, intermediate state, affected artefact, uncertainty, exception, review, and reversal around automated work.

lowPole.label: Hidden autonomy
lowPole.description: The system appears instant and magical, with no visible boundaries, ownership, or recovery.

highPole.label: Observable and governable
highPole.description: People can understand, interrupt, verify, approve, change, and reverse system actions at appropriate risk points.

desiredRange.rationale: Human receivers need trustworthy outputs without carrying an excessive manual review burden.

channelModulation.rationale: Trust claims should reveal representative controls and review points.
Risk-appropriate control, ownership, history, and reversal are product requirements.
Compact proof should avoid implying uncontrolled autonomy and resolve to fuller detail.
Changed state, consequence, responsible party, and next action should be explicit.
Provenance, approval status, uncertainty, and accountable owner support evaluation.

productModulation.rationale: Cross-business orchestration requires visible authority, handoff, exception, and reversal.
Creative selection, claims, budgets, and deployment need explicit approval boundaries.
Interpretation, data quality, method, and confidence need a visible human decision point.
Code changes need plan review, diff visibility, tests, approval, and rollback.

dimensions.confidence: high for the principle, medium for risk thresholds
tensions: Low review burden versus responsible control

tests.passCondition: A reviewer can identify source, owner, permission, change, uncertainty, review, and recovery.

tests.method: Measure review time and error detection with collapsed and expanded controls.
tests.passCondition: Progressive disclosure reduces routine burden without hiding high-risk decisions.

approvalGate.gate: H3 for interaction grammar, per-product risk approval before production
approvalGate.owner: human product owner with design and governance review
approvalGate.requiredEvidence: Risk model, control states, failure storyboard, and reversal behaviour

dimensions.name: Machine portability
dimensions.definition: How reliably approved meaning, behaviour, evidence, and bounded variation transfer between code, Figma, templates, humans, and LLMs through one semantic contract.

lowPole.label: Bespoke and manually mirrored
lowPole.description: Rules live in separate prose, canvas, code, and prompts with hidden context and manual synchronisation.

highPole.label: Registry-driven and validated
highPole.description: Stable IDs, purpose, states, evidence, constraints, mappings, versions, provenance, deprecation, and tests serve every supported renderer.

desiredRange.rationale: LLMs will use the system more than humans, so semantic reliability and bounded variation are core identity requirements.

channelModulation.rationale: Pages should consume approved objects and proof rather than hidden implementation context.
Component API, state, accessibility, and evidence semantics must resolve deterministically.
Creative variation is allowed inside approved claim, source, focal, and brand boundaries.
Content and fallbacks need dependable cross-client rules and canonical claims.
Data, method, source, date, version, and export behaviour require exact transfer.

productModulation.rationale: The flagship should establish the shared semantic registry and orchestration states.
High creative variation needs strict claim, provenance, approval, and export constraints.
Analytical objects and evidence definitions must remain exact across renderers.
Plans, commands, files, diffs, tests, and review states need stable machine contracts.

dimensions.confidence: high for the need, medium for the final architecture
tensions: One source of truth versus renderer-specific requirements

tests.method: Run E-05 with one object in machine contract, human guidance, HTML, Figma mapping, LLM context, and validator.
tests.passCondition: One human and two LLMs create semantically equivalent outputs with bounded visual variation and no hidden context.

tests.method: Change the registry version and deprecate one representation.
tests.passCondition: Every supported consumer identifies the new version, rejects the deprecated form, and preserves provenance.

approvalGate.owner: design systems and engineering leads with human design approval
approvalGate.requiredEvidence: Portability pilot, validator output, versioning proof, and measured review burden
